title_vi: Quản trị truyền thông khủng hoảng
prerequisites: CCO201 or MKT304 or IMC301c or IMC301
description:
This course covers crisis communication theory, crisis management approaches, classic cases and the influence of culture on crisis communication. This course will introduce the definitions of crisis and how they come about, the importance of the Enterprise Risk Management framework in crisis prevention and preparation, and how we can recognise and address crises in case they happen. This course focuses on the role of communications throughout the crisis management process, as well as how to utilise media relations and social media to prevent and/or respond to crises.
Apart from learning academic theories, students will have opportunities to apply their acquired knowledge & skills in analysing a real-world case study, as well as developing a industry-facing crisis communication plan for an organisation ("client") and self-organising an accompanied simulated media conference to address a crisis of that organisation. Throughout that, students will be equipped with practical experience and skills to be ready for their future career path in the communications field.
Finally, students can also use AI to assist their practices and assignemnts.
student_tasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class
- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose
- Read the textbook in advance
- Access the course websites (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

learning_outcomes.details: Identify organisational, industrial and environmental challenges and disasters
Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and practice of issues management and crisis communication.
Utilize AI to analyse and develop strategies for organisational issues using the theories, models and methods of issues management and crisis communication
Gain the capacity to critique organisational and industrial responses to issues and crises in terms of attitude and ethics
Develop a critical attitude towards crisis communications management
Identify and apply ethical standards of practice when dealing with issues management and crisis communication
Skills in analysis and problem solving; AI Literacy and Responsible Communication; Proficient in presentation and teamwork skills; positive contributing attitude in the class and groupworks

assessments.no_question: Evaluative
assessments.grading_guide: Test the acquainted knowledge which student obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapter 1, 6, 7, 8)
assessments.note:
Individual Assessment (At home)
Type: Essay
Weight: 15%
Length: 1,500-2,000 words
Task Description:
Choose from the list of crisis case studies provided by the lecturer before and analyse one organisational crisis.
Your essay will include an overview of the crisis, a description of the organisation, a crisis timeline, actions and responses taken, a media analysis, stakeholder impacts, lessons learned, recommendations, and use appropriate matrix/models.
The essay should address the criteria as outlined in the assessment task and rubric mentioned during the class.
Students should use a mix of scholarly references, media coverage and organisational materials, as well as applying AI-tools to collect information and analyze the chosen crisis.

assessments.question_type: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7
assessments.no_question: The whole class is divided into groups. Each group is assigned to make one crisis communication plan
assessments.grading_guide: Test the acquainted knowledge and skills which student obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapter 1-8, with an emphasis on Chapter 2-5)
assessments.note:
Group Assessment
Type: Crisis Communication Plan (At Home) + Presentation (In the class)
Weight: 25%
Task Description:
Students working within a small group setting of 4-6 students to select one organisation in Vietnam, which must be accepted by the lecturer, then propose a crisis communication plan for that organisation. The plan must showcase all knowledge the students have gained in the class, and be delivered as a final report to their chosen organisation.
AI Application: Students have to demonstrate their capability of applying AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, etc...) in preparing templates in the crisis communication plan, which include (but aren't limited to) prewritten news release(s) and media alert.

Presentation: For the 15-minute presentation, each group have to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates.

Notes:
The detailed structure of a crisis communication plan could be found in the textbook (Chapter 5)
Further details of the crisis communication plan will be provided in class. The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.

assessments.no_question: The whole class is divided into groups. Each group is assigned to create one simulated media conference.
assessments.grading_guide: Test the acquainted knowledge and skills which student obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapter 4-7)
assessments.note:
Group Assessment
Type: Simulated Media Conference (In the class)
Weight: 20%

Based on your crisis communication plan, each group will prepare for a media conference based on the scenario which will respond to a simulated crisis of your chosen organisation. Your media statement should be no more than 15 minutes in total and will be followed by a 15-minute Q&A from the “journalist” members of the class.
Before the media conference, your group have to prepare:
1. a media alert
2. a media kit, including the press release (to be delivered at the conference)
3. a one-page summary of key message
AI Application: Students have to demonstrate their capability of applying AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, etc...) in preparing the above-mentioned documents.

Notes:
Further details of the media conference will be provided in class. The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.

assessments.grading_guide: The questions will cover the lectures, class discussions, activities, exercises, and textbook.

description:
Main objectives:
This course is designed to provide students with essential and working knowledge of the terminology and concepts in the field of consumer behavior and a better understanding of how consumers make choices and how their choices ultimately affect their well-being. After taking this class, the students should all be able to:
(1) Understand basic concepts and major research that has relevance to consumer behaviour
(2) Integrate these concepts into a framework that can be applied to the analysis of the individual consumer and the market
(3) Analyse and understand consumer's decision making process
(4) Apply consumer behaviour in the development and implementation of marketing tactics and strategies.

Description:
This course will review concepts, issues, and methods applicable to the study of consumer behavior. It is divided into 4 main parts: (1) Psychological characteristics of consumers; (2) Social and external factors influencing consumer behavior; (3) The role of sub-culture and culture; and (4) Consumer decision-making process.
Class discussions, case study analysis , practical activities, along with group projects and quizzes will provide the basis for the learning environment in the classroom.
The assignment requires students to integrate AI throughout the project, leveraging it for ideation, structuring, content generation, and analysis. The primary level of using AI is "AI Task Completion, Human Evaluation", with creative aspects edging into the "Full AI", as students rely on AI to achieve creative outputs collaboratively while critically engaging with its results.

description:
The course empowerC14ommon Adobe 2D tools for Multimedia designers, which are Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign and Xd, so that they can finalize their 2D designs better and able to deliver completed professional product to customers
Through practical assignments, students have chances to apply knowledge on colors, typography etc. in other courses along with computers and other tools to creaate graphic applications. In addition, students will be introduced to the application of AI tools in design workflows, developing AI literacy to enhance creativity and collaboration. The course also emphasizes the cultivation of a professional attitude and working style, preparing students for real-world design projects and industry practices.
student_tasks:
- Read textbook and install software before coming to class
- Complete assignments in class, submit online thoughout LMS or Classroom platform.
- Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course.
- Actively participate into class, review and comments to classmate works, ask instructor questions, bring into class everyday samples for references.
- Complete homework and other requirements by instructors
- Using laptop in class only for taking note, research and doing assignment purposes
- No talking, surfing, chatting, gaming, facebooking, using phone etc. while the teacher giving instruction.
- Present at least 80% class attendance in order to pass the course.
tools:
1. The school prepare: (Installed)

2. Student prepare:
- Note/Sketchbooks, pens and pencils
- Laptop for graphic design with Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator and Indesign installed
- Suitable Generative AI tools

Students are required to use their personal account (not the university or organizational account) to register for an Adobe account.

learning_outcomes.details: Understanding of vector, bitmap, and layout principles, together with essential design principles as the basis for creating effective 2D design products.
Apply Adobe Illustrator proficiently to create vector-based design products such as logos, icons, and illustrations…
Apply Adobe Photoshop proficiently to develop bitmap-based design products such as photo edits, digital paintings, and visual effects…
Apply Adobe InDesign proficiently to produce layout-based publishing products such as brochures, magazines, and posters…
Apply AI tools and demonstrate AI literacy to collaborate effectively.
Having a positive attitude and a professional working style.

assessments.no_question:
Students will receive the assignment instructions and requirements directly from the instructor.
The task is to design a vector-based graphic product (ex: logo, icon, pattern, or vector illustration...) using Adobe Illustrator.

Students are provided with a sample vector-based graphic product or may propose one for instructor approval.
Students are required to reproduce the product using Illustrator tools and submit the work at the end of the session.
Submission includes the original working file (.AI), and exported outputs in required formats.
assessments.grading_guide:
Master basic and advanced Illustrator tools for vector drawing.
Develop the ability to transform creative concepts into vector-based products: logo, icon, pattern, vector illustration.

assessments.question_type: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7, CLO8
assessments.no_question:
Students will receive the assignment instructions and requirements directly from the instructor.
Create a media graphic product: poster, social media content, promotional design... using Adobe Photoshop.
AI integration.
Option 1 (AI as Idea Partner)
Students will use one or more AI tools to generate ideas for a specific media graphic product.
Students are then required to recreate the AI-generated idea using Photoshop tools.
Submission must include: Original Photoshop working file (.PSD), exported outputs in the required formats and documentation of the AI-generated idea.

Option 2 ( AI as Creative Element Generator):
Students may first propose their own product idea, discuss and confirm it with instructor.
After idea approval, students will use Photoshop to create the final product, while being allowed to use AI tools to generate supporting elements.
Submission must include: Original Photoshop working file (.PSD), exported outputs in the required formats and documentation of the AI-generated idea.
assessments.grading_guide:
Use Photoshop tools effectively for image editing, photo manipulation, and digital compositing.
Produce creative outputs such as posters, social media graphics, or promotional materials.

assessments.no_question:
Students will receive the assignment instructions and requirements directly from the instructor.
Design a layout project:brochure, magazine spread, or template for digital or print publishing...

Students will be given a layout brief or may propose one for instructor approval.
Students are required to complete the assignment using InDesign.
AI tools may be applied responsibly for supporting tasks such as generating placeholder text, sample images, illustration...
Submission must include InDesign working file (.INDD), exported outputs in required formats, packaged file folder, printed version (if requested), documentation of the idea development process and AI-generated content.
assessments.grading_guide:
Demonstrate proficiency in using InDesign tools effectively.
Create professional layout projects such as magazines, brochures, and templates for print or digital publishing.

description:
The course is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in marketing based on five key activities: (1) identifying customer needs, (2) providing customers with the right products or service to meet their needs, (3) assuring availability to customers through the right distribution channels, (4) using promotional activities in ways that motivate purchase as effectively as possible, (5) setting an appropriate price that maximizes firm profitability while maintaining customer satisfaction.
The Principle of Marketing course (Philip Kotler) integrates AI tools as supportive instruments for idea generation, document organization, and the practical application of marketing concepts. Students will employ AI for brainstorming, content structuring, creation of marketing materials, and basic analytics, while retaining full responsibility for ensuring originality, critical evaluation, and refinement of their work. The course also equips students to assess the strengths and limitations of AI-generated outputs and to identify ethical risks such as plagiarism and bias.
Tools Utilized:
- lmarena AI: For generating marketing-related data and insights.
- Statista: For accessing statistical data and market research.
- ChatGPT: For idea generation, structuring documents, and simulating real-life marketing scenarios.
- Canva: For creating visual marketing materials like infographics, templates, and videos.
The assessment methods have been reformed to more accurately reflect students’ actual competencies. Learners are evaluated through oral examinations, presentations, group debates, and the assessment of submitted products, as well as through their selection of prompts, which demonstrate their thinking process, revisions, and interactions with AI feedback.

description: Introduction to International Business is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles and practices of conducting business in a globalized economy. It explores the dynamic interplay of socio-cultural, economic, technological, and political-legal factors that shape the international business environment. Students will gain insights into the strategies and techniques for entering and operating in foreign markets, including trade policies, global supply chains, and cross-border management. A key feature of this course is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and applications, enabling students to analyze international market trends, optimize decision-making processes, and develop innovative solutions to real-world business challenges. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to navigate the complexities of international business with a forward-thinking, technology-driven approach.

description:
This course explores the central concepts of organisational procurement, global sourcing and interfaces of these to the other areas of an organisation. This course provides opportunities to examine issues such as organisational procurement process, global sourcing process, supplier selection process, supplier management and other strategic issues.
*Teaching method: This is a blended-learning course, in which students will take a look at the videos & slides and reading on Coursera first at home, then rewatch & discuss key questions with classmates and teachers at classes.
AI Tools will be used to support students in
(1) generating ideas/structures for their speaking notes and slide structure of important topics of the course.
(2) editing the slide set after students have already finished it.
student_tasks:
- Access the learning materials on Coursera for self-study purposes
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be eligible for the final assessment
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class
- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose
- Access FU FLM at http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.details: demonstrate basic understanding of procurement of an enterprise
practice the ability to conduct negotiation in procurement
demonstrate proficiency in applying AI tools to develop solutions to professional issues
demonstrate understanding of stakeholder management in the given context of an enterprise
analyze the 7-step Strategic Sourcing Process
demonstrate the ability to select and evaluate supplier
practice the ability to develop a supplier evaluation system for an enterprise
discuss various types of contracts that can be used in procurement
demonstrate understanding of risk in procurement and the ability to mitigate it
discuss some ethical considerations in procurement
apply tools to evaluate a Supply Market from Macro, Industry, and Supplier Level

description: Economics is the study of how the society manages its scarce resources. Economics has been divided into the subcategories of microeconomics and macroeconomics. While macroeconomics studies aggregate issues related to national and international economic activities, this course - microeconomics - focuses on the behavior of individual economic agents. Microeconomics studies how households (or individuals), business (or firms, enterprises) and the government make decisions, given scarcity of resources. It also studies the interactions among those market members and how these interactions have impacts on their economic benefits and the economy. Because most of these activities occur in the markets, this course also focuses on how the markets work.

learning_outcomes.details: Explain why consumers attempt to maximize utility.
Shows self-reliance when working independently and collaboratively
Demonstrate ethical awareness and reflection in business context
Describe long runs and short runs
Discuss fixed, variable, and total costs
Identify the characteristics of microeconomics and its effect consumers, businesses, and owners
Recognize the three primary forms of elasticity as their impacts on economics
Review curve analysis and how it reflects consumer demand
Apply utility theory to the changing world of supply and demand
Describe cost curves and consumer variables
Recognize the role of supply and demand in economics, government policies.

description: The course explores and focuses around the managerial functions of management, including planning, organizing, leading and controlling. The course is designed to provide basic knowledge and skills required in management and give students a comprehensive insight into human relations componnents that characterise any managerial roles, regardless of industry or functions. Various aspects of management theories will be examined and linked to current management practice in the world and Vietnam. Learning in the class will be facilitated through the use of interactive tools such as group exercise, case study discussion, role-play/activities, and projects.

learning_outcomes.details: Define management, its functions including planning, decision-making, and strategy development processes, and influence of organizational environments.
Describe the basic elements of organization design, encompassing forms, key situational influences, and components involved in designing effective operations systems.
Discuss human resource management practices, including recruitment, development, motivation, and leadership strategies, within the context of environmental factors.
Identify different types of organizational control mechanisms and analyze their characteristics to determine effectiveness in achieving organizational objectives.
Apply the knowledge and understanding gained from the course to evaluate real-life management situations/dilemma and practices in both local and global business contexts.
Develop leadership and management potential through the integration of theoretical knowledge with practical skills and self-awareness.
Understand the ethical and social responsibility issues in real-life management situations.

description:
1. Môn học này nhằm giúp sinh viên nâng cao kỹ năng giao tiếp bằng tiếng Trung, đặc biệt là các kỹ năng giao tiếp hàng ngày trong cuộc sống và trong công việc.
2. Thông qua các chủ đề gần gũi với cuộc sống hàng ngày như cách làm quen, cách chia sẻ quan điểm, cách nghĩ của mình về các vấn đề như sức khỏe, ẩm thực, mua sắm, sở thích, thói quen, cách hỏi thông tin, cách thương lượng…, người học sẽ nắm vững được các cấu trúc và từ vựng ở trình độ tiền trung cấp, và biết cách vận dụng các kiến thức được học vào các tình huống giao tiếp mô phỏng, từ đó nâng cao khả năng nghe nói tiếng Trung.

- Chuẩn bị bài trước giờ học (học trước từ vựng, làm bài tập, chuẩn bị các nội dung cần thiết tùy theo từng buổi).
- Tích cực tham gia vào giờ học trên lớp, hoàn thành bài tập giảng viên giao.
- Tích cực trao đổi thông tin với giảng viên để hoàn thành tốt môn học.

learning_outcomes.details: 【Kiến thức ngôn ngữ - văn hóa】Hiểu và ghi nhớ được cách viết, cách đọc, ý nghĩa của khoảng hơn 600 từ vựng và các phần chú thích ngữ pháp, vận dụng được các phần từ mới và ngữ pháp đã học trong các tình huống giao tiếp phù hợp về các chủ đề gần gũi với đời sống hàng ngày như: giới thiệu bản thân và tìm hiểu về người khác, tìm kiếm và chia sẻ thông tin, cách giải quyết vấn đề khi gặp khó khăn, mẫu thuẫn...

【Kỹ năng ngôn ngữ】 Nghe hiểu và trả lời được các câu hỏi liên quan tới các đoạn hội thoại mô phỏng các tình huống giao tiếp trong đời sống hàng ngày hoặc các đoạn văn ngắn về các chủ đề đã học. Đọc hiểu được các nội dung bài khóa và bài tập trong giáo trình Vận dụng được các kiến thức đã học để tiến hành hội thoại, tóm tắt lại các nội dung bài học và thảo luận về các chủ đề được giới thiệu trong giáo trình
【Kỹ năng mềm】Có khả năng làm việc độc lập, làm việc nhóm, có khả năng nhìn nhận các vấn đề đa chiều, có tư duy phản biện.

title_vi: Tiếng Nhật công nghệ thông tin
prerequisites: Từ K20A: Passed JST301 K19: Passed JTS301 K18 trở về trước: Passed JJB391 JS: Passed JPD316
description:
Môn học giúp sinh viên chuyên ngành Nhật ngữ khi ra trường có thể làm việc tại các công ty Nhật Bản chuyên về IT . Nội dung của môn học sẽ bao gồm 2 yếu tố chính sau:
1. Cung cấp các kiến thức cơ bản liên quan đến Công nghệ thông tin bằng tiếng Nhật như những kiến thức cơ bản về máy tính, sử dụng internet, các thiết bị IT, công nghệ truyền dữ liệu, an toàn và bảo mật, cấu trúc máy tính, cơ sở dữ liệu, lập trình, cấu trúc dữ liệu và giải thuật.... .
2. Bổ sung lượng từ vựng, các thuật ngữ và các biểu đạt liên quan đến công nghệ thông tin, giúp sinh viên luyện tập để có thể đọc, hiểu, và dịch tốt các nội dung, các văn bản thuộc lĩnh vực này.
student_tasks:
- Học viên cần phải tham gia tối thiểu 80% số tiết để đủ điều kiện thi cuối khóa
- Học viên cần phải học từ vựng trước khi tham gia lớp học
- Học viên có thể sử dụng laptop trong lớp học cho mục đích học tập .
tools: Giáo trình chính (情報技術日本語テキスト — ベトナム人学習者向け　— (2013年) ), Tài liệu do giảng viên cung cấp

learning_outcomes.details: Hiểu được kiến thức cơ bản về công nghệ thông tin như Hệ điều hành, CSDL, Cơ sở lập trình, mô tả dữ liệu, truyền dữ liệu …
Hiểu được tên gọi các thiết bị máy tính cũng như cấu trúc của máy vi tính
Nắm bắt được các nguyên lý cơ bản trong kỹ thuật công nghệ thông tin về phần cứng và phần mềm
Nắm bắt được cách sử dụng Internet, Internet thương mại, công nghệ internet
Nắm được kiến thức mạng và quy tắc an toàn bảo mật mạng…
Hiểu được các giải thuật cơ bản trong công nghệ thông tin
Hiểu được các xử lý tính toán cơ bản trong công nghệ thông tin
Có thể biết cách làm việc cũng như tác phong làm việc trong công ty Công nghệ thông tin Nhật Bản
Hiểu được các thuật ngữ chuyên ngành công nghệ thông tin bằng tiếng Nhật và dịch được văn bản chuyên ngành công nghệ thông tin

prerequisites: Từ K20A: Passed JST301 K19,K18D: Passed JTS301 K18C trở về trước: Passed JJB391 JS: Passed JPD316
description:
Là một trong những môn học lựa chọn trong định hướng CNTT được triển khai vào sau giai đoạn OJT cho những sinh viên có định hướng về CNTT.
Tại thời điểm này sinh viên đã hoàn thành khối kiến thức kĩ năng tiếng, chuyên ngành và đi vào chuyên ngành sâu CNTT.
Môn học cung cấp:
- Từ vựng chuyên ngành CNTT trong ngành phần mềm.
- Cách diễn đạt trong triển khai dự án.
- Tình huống thực tế đã được sử dụng trong các dự án phần mềm (tình huống giao tiếp, tình huống đặt ra khi tham gia dự án phần mềm)
Môn học giúp sinh viên từng bước làm quen để sau khi tốt nghiệp có thể tham gia vào dự án phần mềm.
student_tasks:
- Học viên cần phải tham gia tối thiểu 80% số tiết để đủ điều kiện thi cuối khóa.
- Học viên có thể sử dụng laptop trong lớp học cho mục đích học tập .
- Tập sự nghiên cứu, tìm hiểu về các vấn đề có liên quan tiếng Nhật CNTT trong ngành phần mềm.
- Ôn tập bài giảng, đối chiếu với slide bài học để nắm vững các kiến thức và từ vựng liên quan đến tiếng Nhật CNTT trong ngành phần mềm.
- Trên lớp tích cực tham gia trao đổi, thảo luận về chủ đề được đưa ra.
- Hoàn thành các bài tập thực hành liên quan đến nội dung bài giảng.
tools: Giáo trình chính ( Tiếng Nhật Công Nghệ Thông Tin trong ngành phần mềmーITの日本語ソフトウェア開発プロジェクトー (2022年) ), Tài liệu do giảng viên cung cấp

materials.note: Thư viện cung cấp bản online cho sinh viên

learning_outcomes.details: Hiểu được những kiến thức cơ bản về chu trình, công đoạn, các tình huống giao tiếp thực tế của một dự án phát triển phần mềm
Hiểu được các thuật ngữ, các cách diễn đạt hay dùng trong dự án phát triển phần mềm bằng tiếng Nhật và dịch được văn bản chuyên ngành liên quan đến dự án phát triển phần mềm
Hiểu được nội dung công việc, các tài liệu liên quan sử dụng trong dự án phát triển phần mềm
Hiểu và có thể làm việc bằng tiếng Nhật với các đối tác là công ty CNTT Nhật Bản
Hiểu được cách làm việc cũng như tác phong làm việc trong công ty CNTT Nhật Bản
Có thái độ nghiêm túc, nhiệt tình, hợp tác và tác phong làm việc chuyên nghiệp khi tham gia vào dự án phát triển phần mềm

description: This Specialization covers marketing concepts but, more importantly, emphasizes the need by companies and individuals to think openly across international markets and industries for new ideas or expansion. This is summarized as "Cross Country & Cross Industry" Innovation, or CCCI in short. The first two courses will establish the core foundations and then the last three courses will elaborate on major global industry clusters: course 3 on B2B, course 4 on Healthcare and Hospitality, and course 5 on Sports and Entertainment. The capstone will require learners to develop a new product using knowledge learned from at least 2 industries.

3. Respect the Coursera Code of Conduct, at https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/208280036-Coursera-Code-of-Conduct
3. Keep online learning progress promptly (bonus will be awarded)
4. Communicate and discuss in forum
5. Attend off-line sessions in the Campus (Optional)
6. Must complete all MOOCs of spec. with certification in order to take the Final Exam at Campus

description: This course is designed to teach students to optimize website content for the best possible search engine ranking. Students will learn the theory behind Google search and other search engine algorithms, as well as build practical, real-world skills that can be applied to a career in digital marketing or online content development, including on-page and off-page optimization, optimizing for local and international audiences, conducting search-focused website audits, and aligning SEO with overall business strategies. Students will also learn how to create and execute search campaigns on Google Ads Search (formally AdWords). Through an introductory overview, students are guided through the official Google Ads Search training materials. Beyond Google materials, practical campaign creation and optimization best practices and exercises are provided to ensure the acquisition of practical skills and knowledge.

description:
Description: This course is based on the Coursera Specialization "Digital Marketing," offering a comprehensive exploration of the dynamics and global aspects of digital marketing. Students will delve into how the Digital Revolution has impacted marketing in an Analog World and gain insights into the core processes of planning and executing a digital marketing campaign.
Additionally, the course integrates the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to equip students with essential skills for market data collection, consumer behavior analysis, and effective digital marketing strategy development. By the end of the course, students will be able to select the most suitable marketing channels for various products and design impactful AI-powered digital campaigns.
*Teaching Method: This blended-learning course combines self-paced online study with collaborative in-class activities. Students are required to review videos, slides, and readings on Coursera before class. During class sessions, they will review key content and engage with peers and instructors to reinforce and apply their knowledge.

description:
This Course is based on the both Coursera Specialization "The Strategy of Content Marketing" and "Social Media Management", which covers both the theorical and practical lessons of content marketing. You firstly will learn the core strategies content marketers use to acquire and retain customers profitably. Specifically, you will learn how to develop, organize and implement a content marketing strategy, analyze and measure the effectiveness of content marketing, write compelling copy, use a strategic framework when writing, and build your professional brand and authority through content marketing. You will also learn how to put the ideas presented to you into action and build your own personal brand through content marketing. You will end the course with real-world application of your skills through a content management project on social media.
This is a blended-learning course, in which students will take a look at the videos & slides and reading on Coursera first at home, then rewatch & discuss key questions with classmates and teachers at classes.
AI tools can significantly enhance content marketing efforts by automating tasks, improving content quality, and providing valuable insights. Some AI tools that can be used in content marketing include:
AI Writing Tools, AI Design Tools, AI Social Media Management Tools, AI Analytics Tools

description:
A supply chain is comprised of all the parties involved in fulfilling a customer request. The integrated management of this network is a critical determinant of success in today’s competitive environment.
Supply chain management is the systemic, strategic coordination of the traditional business functions within a particular company and across businesses within a supply chain, for the purpose of improving the long-term performance of the individual companies and the supply chain as a whole. The major supply chain processes include planning, sourcing, making or converting, fulfillment, and relationships management. The major dimensions for evaluating the performance of supply chain processes and activities are time, cost, quality and compliance. This course covers the major activities of companies involved in profitably coordinating supply and demand in the marketplace to deliver consumer value.

description: Economics is the study of how society manages its scarce resources. Economics has been divided into the subcategories of microeconomics and macroeconomics. While microeconomics focuses on the behavior of individual economic agents, this course - macroeconomics - studies how economists measure macroeconomic variables and covers topics such as determination of national output, economic growth, unemployment, inflation, interest rates, and exchange rates. Macroeconomics also discusses and assesses the effectiveness of monetary and fiscal policies under different scenarios.

description:
The course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of both classical and contemporary marketing theories, as well as their practical applications. Throughout the course, students will engage with new classical and contemporary cases, exploring the interdisciplinary and cross-functional implications of business management theories, contemporary marketing management principles, and futuristic applications of marketing management theories and concepts. Upon successful completion of this course, students shall:
1. Acquire an understanding of the significance of management and marketing in various organisational settings.
2. Gain a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles that govern management and marketing.
3. Demonstrate outstanding analytic abilities that are critical for effectively tackling obstacles in business and marketing operations and reaching well-informed managerial judgements.
student_tasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Student is responsible to do all exercises, questions, assignments given by instructor(s)/ lecturer(s) in class or at home and submit on time
- Use laptop in class only for learning purposes
- Promptly access to the FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.details: Display comprehensive understanding of marketing terminology and concepts.
Demonstrate proficiency in utilizing marketing and marketing mix components strategically.
Define management, management functions and management process
Discuss human resource management practices, including recruitment, development, motivation, and leadership strategies
Develop effective communication strategies based on an understanding of and the ability to apply marketing terminology and concepts.
Show professionalism, ethical behavior, and social responsibility while collaborating effectively on group projects.

assessments.no_question:
Opt.1: Group Project.
Suggested topic: Analyse the unique marketing challenges faced by an actual company. Suggestions to augment the marketing efficacy of the organisation shall be furnished, drawing upon theoretical frameworks acquired throughout the course. Observations, in-depth interviews with company administrators and personnel, and a comprehensive review of the organization's documents will all contribute to the development of this assignment.

Opt.2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

description:
-Main objective: The aim of this subject is to integrate knowledge with front office, housekeeping and others relevant departments in accommodation and apply them to problem solving in the areas of room division management. The course provides learners the necessary knowledge and skills to become a room division manager.
-Description: During the course, students are practiced to design a room division department, apply the plan in real operation. Learners will be trained in management skills in several key aspects of room division management including operational administration, human resource management and departmental revenue optimization.
-Teaching method: Lecture, Desmontration, Role Play, Project based learning, Cooperative Learning

- Respect and protect school asset.
- Strongly communication and teamworking.

title_vi: Nghiệp vụ tiền sảnh, lễ tân
description:
Main objective: The course aims for equipping students hands-on experiences as real front office employees through handle variety of tasks in each position under front office department.
Description: Taking school laboratory with standard of 3 star hotel as a real working environment, Front office management 2 focuses particularly on training practical skills in front office deparment for students. The course allows student to experience detailed daily tasks of each position cross front office department such as receptionist, phone operator, cashier, night auditor…etc…With various day to day situation to deal and to handle, learner will be familiar with front office operations enhancing competitive advantage on the hotel job market.
-Teaching method: lecture, discussion, demonstration, roleplay, project based learning, group work
- Facility and equipment requirement : Depending on the training condition of each campus, the course will be implemented in school lab designed up to 4-5* hotel standard, real hotel or other places, which fully met with requirements.
student_tasks:
Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class
- Comply with the time and regulation
- Professional grooming
- Respect and protect school asset.
- Strongly communication and teamworking.

materials.author: Michael L. Kasavana, Ph.D
materials.publisher: The American Hotel & Lodging Educational Institute (AHLEI)

learning_outcomes.details: Demonstrate highly cooperation and discipline the team, instructor and school regulation
Present a professional and courtesy reception style
Understand and know how to use hotel management system
Explain the reservation concept & procedure and master receptionist profession
Describe and master bell and concierge profession
Comprend and master the phone operator functions
Analyze and solve situations skillfully in reservation and guest relation service.
Explain and perform front office cashier function.
Explain and execute the night audit function
Communicate fluently and confidently in english in every guest services tasks

assessments.no_question: Role Plays, PPTs presentation, Performance video record.
assessments.grading_guide: Chapter 1-7
assessments.note:
Role Play in lab and presentation' submission via email or anycourse supporting platfrom.

Group Assignment Suggestion:
Students will be seperated into the team of 5 to10 people. The team is expected to operate the front office division as the standard of 5 star hotels. The teams will select the hotel brand by their own based on history, design concept, room categories, favorite service style. The groups will divide members themselves to ensure each menber cover a role in the front office division from Fom to cashier, bell, receptionist…. On the day of performance, the team will manage unexpected situations given by lecturers or other group students altogether. Before practical day, the teams must submit a presentation with the content of hotel name, information, characteristics,philosophy, design, service style and team members.
Grading is based on performance in class (70%), check point quality (10%), ppts presentation (20%).
The performance should be filmed for review.

assessments.grading_guide: - To create a disciplined environment and maintain a professional interface as a internationl hotelier standard, It is manatory for student to follow two indispensible aspects in service industry as a grading criteria, which are attitude and professional grooming.
assessments.note:
Students must comply perfectly with school & class regulation such as grooming, uniform, personal hygiene and attitude coming to demo front office with details the following:
1. Attitude
- Work seriously and attentively
- Respect and protect school asset.
- Strongly communication and teamworking.
- Be on time with professional grooming
2. Dress & Grooming Code
For Boys:
- School uniform or personal clothes including Black Trousers, White Shirt Full Sleeves, Tie or Vest
(Entering class with Jeans & T shirts is not allowed)
-The sleeves of a full sleeve shirt should never be rolled up.
- Formal shoes (black) and black socks.
- No Ear rings, bangles except for religious purpose are allowed in the class.
- Any kind of hair dye and spike hair style is strictly prohibited.
- In winter black coat and black pullover.
- Wearing of Name tag is mandatory for all students during class
For Girls:
- School Uniform or personal clothes such as Black Trousers, White Shirt Full Sleeves, Vest or Ao dai
(Entering class with Jeans & T shirts is not allowed)
- The sleeves of shirt should never be rolled up.
- Formal black shoes with ankle high socks.
- No visible painting including mehendi and tattoos.
- Only one ear ring/top.
- In winter black coat and black cardigan without collar are allowed.
- Hair should be tied in Bun shape during class.

assessments.grading_guide:
PT1: Chapter 1
'PT2: Chapter 2,3,4
'PT3: Chapter 5,6,7
assessments.note:
Practical Test Suggestion:
-PT1: Using computer and PMS on lab to handle situations according to the examination request.

-PT2: Each students select randomly a procedure of chapter 2,3,4. After selection each student will be grouped into teams of 8-10 people (arranged randomly) and perform their own procedure at the same time on lab. Grade will be scored individually based on the proficiency and professionalism of the procedure that the student has performed.

-PT3: Each students select randomly a procedure of chapter 5,6,7. After selection each student will be grouped into teams of 8-10 people (arranged randomly) and perform their own procedure at the same time on lab. Grade will be scored individually based on the proficiency and professionalism of the procedure that the student has performed.

assessments.no_question:
Multiple choices
Marked by Computer
assessments.grading_guide: Chapter 1-7

title_vi: Quản lý tiền sảnh, lễ tân
description:
This course consists of the study of hotel front office procedures, with the primary focus is the front office, housekeeping, reservations, and night audit departments. Other departments are discussed to provide and understanding of how these departments relate to the front office and how they operate to enhance the guest experience. The course gives students a real world understanding of the hotel industry balancing its past, present and future. It reveals the inner workings of a hotel in a way that both promotes learning and interest for the students, preparing them for what to expect in the current and future hotel market.
-Description:The course focuses on the front office, housekeeping, F&B and how they relate to each other in order to provide excellent service to customers. Other departments are also explained to provide a full understanding of the organization of a hotel. Students are to practice their analyzing and problem solving skills with up-to-date real life example and current trends.
-Teaching method: lecture, discussion, demonstration, roleplay, project based learning, group work
- Facility and equipment requirement : Depending on the training condition of each campus, the course will be implemented in school lab designed up to 4-5* hotel standard, real hotel or other places, which fully met with requirements.

3) Completion Criteria:
Every on-going assessment component > 0; Final Result >=5 & Final Exam Score >= 4

description:
In order to remain competitive, hospitality organizations of today, in particularly highend hotels are very much focused on the “guest experience”. They are under high
pressure to deliver high service standards as today’s consumers are looking for more
value for their money. This course covers the topic of managing hospitality organizations by using academic studies and real life experiences from companies and is written in three sections: Strategy, Staffing and Systems. Each chapter includes at suggested hospitality activities for students, in which students are encourages to visit local organizations to talk with guests, employees and managers to obtain a variety of perspectives on the guest experience.

description:
This course helps students answer three important questions: what is event public relations, why do we do it, and how do we do it?
This course applies the knowledge and skills needed by a public relations practitioner to design, organize and publish a special event as part of a broader public relations program or as an independent communication tool. Students will learn how to execute a PR campaign for an event and how to effectively lead and motivate a team. Students also participate in practical training to organize an event.
- Instructors will use a number of teaching methods such as group discussions and experience sharing, practical work practice instead of conventional teaching.
- Students will have the opportunity to present their work and thought processes related to this work.
student_tasks:
- Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to participate the PR campaign pitch for event.
- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time
- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose

Task Description:
The critical essay is intended to help students identify basic concepts and principles of effective public relations by analysing a key development, change or issue applied to the field of PR and professional communication.
Students will choose a topic, from the list provided, or they may provide a detailed topic of their own to be cleared in writing by the lecturer. The topics are intended to justify some of the themes covered in the course and provide them with the opportunity to gain their knowledge and examine how their topic impacts on society, publics, consumers and professional practice.
Notes:
Students should provide clear illustrations/examples in their essay to show their understanding of the topic.
All topics are written as a draft. Lecturers have the privilege to change the content of each topic as much as they want.
Choose one from the following essay topics:
Topic 1: What are the pros and cons of using a celebrity as part of a promotional event?
Topic 2: Describe the work of an entertainment publicist. Would you be interested in applying for the job of press coordinator?
Topic 3: Why is it important for event executives to have a good relationship with the mass media? How can you as a PR professional facilitate that relationship?

Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

The course demonstrates concepts, technology, and applications of advanced event planning.
2. Course Content:
Key topics include: Overview of the event knowledge on planning, operations, marketing, finance, legal aspects, and specialized event types, incorporating practical skills. Additionally, it includes a new module on the application of Artificial Intelligence in event management, equipping students with cutting-edge technological insights to enhance event design, logistics, and marketing.
3. Activities and Teaching Methodology:
Lectures, hands-on sessions, and individual and group projects will help students practice and develop the knowledge and management skill about event industry.

title_vi: Sự kiện đặc biêt và tổ chức tiệc cưới
description:
-Objective: To provide an overall and in-depth competence of wedding planning and management
-Description: It gives a comprehensive and in-depth knowlodege of different aspects of wedding planning and management, starting from supplying a strong foundation knowledge in the cultural, historical, social, and political influences on weddings and marriage; to accommodating with all of the elements essential to the practice of planning weddings; as well as a clear overview of what it takes to start a wedding consulting business.
-Teaching method: lecturing in combination with tutorial classes, case study analysis, real event planning practice
student_tasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class
- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose
- Read the textbook in advance
- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

materials.description: Wedding planning & management: consultancy for diverse clients
materials.author: Daniels, M. & Loveless, C.

learning_outcomes.details: To get an insight into the role of the wedding consultants and their appreciation of and sensitivity to the diverse needs of the clients
To establish the cultural, religious, historical, political and social context of the weddings
To examine the individual fundamental elements that together lead to the design and implementation of weddings
To develop procedures for the weddings and manage resources and logistics to ensure weddings are delivered in line with event plans
To monitor and evaluate events to ensure customer and business requirements are met
To achieve and practice a professional manner of an event planner with high sense of responsibility, detail orientedness, servicemind and teamwork spirit

Option 1: -Students working in a team to make wedding plan for a real or potential couple (friends, relatives, celebrities...)
- Each team will do the research about the couple, their style, situation to develop a master plan, operational plans, procedure and design for their wedding
- The team has to develop different checklists and tools to control and evaluate the wedding and continously update with and get the feedback from the clients

title_vi: Hội nghị và Hội chợ thương mại
description:
-Objective: Upon the rapid growth of the meeting, expositions, events and conventions industry (MEEC), the subject is aimed to provide an introduction to the MEEC industry and an opportunity for the learner to describe, analyse and evaluate the resources required to organise an MEEC, basing on that to develop a full plan and to implement an event.
-Description: It gives a comprehensive overview of the burgeoning field of planning and producing MEEC — meetings, expositions, events, and conventions with the study of varied segments of the field, along with discussions of new trends.
-Teaching method: lecturing in combination with case study analysis, MEEC practice
student_tasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class
- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose
- Read the textbook in advance
- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

materials.description: Meetings, Expositions, Events, and Conventions: An Introduction to the Industry
materials.author: Fenich G. G.

learning_outcomes.details: To describe the profession and the structure of the MEEC industry
To critically identify the role and functions of each key player in the MEEC industry, including organisers, sponsors, DMOs, venues, contractors, destination management companies
To examine the use of facilities for meetings and conventions
To clarify the structure of and the organisation issues in the exhibition sector
To analyse different planning elements in MEEC industry, including food & beverage, legal issue, technology, green issue, international issues
To develop and implement a full plan for an MEEC of different aspects
To build a professional manner as an MEEC planner

assessments.no_question: Each student shoud make at least 1 individual presentation/ case analysis during the course in front of the class.
assessments.note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

title_vi: Phát triển sản phẩm du lịch
description:
Objective:
Students understand the various components that contribute to the design of a tourism product, such as local culture, important holidays, nearby resorts, modes of transportation, the availability of intermediary service providers, and the development prospects of that tourism product in the country's tourism industry's future. Students must generate an idea, create a product, and persuade the class that it is effective, viable, sustainable, and has the potential for development, in which students must present analysis of the strategic products of various organizations using case studies.

Description:
This course teaches the structure, functions, operations, strategies, and other aspects of tourism goods, as well as how to build and implement one or more comprehensive tourism products. The course also analyzes and provides information on specific tourism items such as specific fascination, cultural, religious, and so forth. The course also includes real-life case studies on tourism product design.
student_tasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class
- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes
- Read the textbook in advance
- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

materials.author: M. R. Dileep

materials.author: Simon Hudson & Louise Hudson

learning_outcomes.details: Define and analyze the extent of services, evaluate the relevance of services in the economy as a whole, and tourism services in particular.
Distinguish between the marketing mix for tangible products and the marketing mix for intangible services, and investigate the use of service in tourism.
Understand all of the aspects that drive tourism product ideation, design, and implementation, such as destination selection, culture, entertainment, and so on.
Investigate the processes of tourism product development, from concept design to actual execution, as well as the method of tourism product operation.
Understand several fundamental and unique forms of tourist products, such as cultural, religious, resort, beach, and event types, among others.
Define a communication and promotion strategy to extensively spread typical tourism products and stress the sustainability of tourism products using communication methods.
Analyze and evaluate several organizations' tourism product strategies using common case studies.
Develop products that address contemporary issues in the development of tourist products for events, resorts, cruises, and other tourism products.
Acquire professional attitudes and abilities to obtain an understanding of designing tourism products for a wide range of customers.

assessments.note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.no_question: Written report and presentation
assessments.knowledge_and_skill:
Written report: limitation of 4000 words
Presentation: 30 mins/group
assessments.grading_guide: All Topics
assessments.note:
Each group comprises of four to five students who prepare and present to the class a creative and one-of-a-kind tourist product for their travel company.

The report must be a synthesis of a creative idea, an academic strategic analysis and a realisticl business plan. Students are encouraged to apply all the knowledge and skills gained from the course to design a tourism product.

If the submission product is found to be a product produced/designed by another party, the student will fail this assignment.
Students are required to provide written and oral reports.

description:
Objectives: This course cultivates a comprehensive skillset for students aspiring to thrive in the dynamic field of tour operations. Graduates will emerge proficient in crafting compelling itineraries, implementing effective marketing and sales strategies, and navigating the intricacies of financial management and risk mitigation. Furthermore, the course fosters the development of critical thinking and problem-solving abilities, alongside strong communication skills and a commitment to ethical conduct – all essential for a flourishing career in the ever-evolving tourism industry.

Description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to tour operations and management. Students will gain a thorough understanding of the key concepts and practical skills involved in crafting, organizing, and executing successful tours for travelers.
student_tasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfill tasks given by the instructor after class
- Use laptop in class only for learning purposes
- Read the textbook in advance
- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

materials.description: Tour operators and operations: development, management and responsibility
materials.author: J. Holland, D. Leslie

learning_outcomes.details: To articulate the core principles and evolving landscape of tour management within the tourism industry (combines concepts, roles, importance & trends).
Craft comprehensive tour itineraries through a strategic selection of destinations, transportation, accommodation, dining, and sightseeing experiences.
Employ effective sales techniques to captivate potential clients in tourism industry
Deliver exceptional customer service by adeptly handling feedback and resolving complaints with professionalism.
Master tour budgeting, cost management, and cash flow control to ensure financial viability.
Develop superior communication and problem-solving skills to navigate tour operations effectively.
Think critically and adapt by proposing creative solutions to unforeseen challenges and making decisive actions during tours.

assessments.note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.no_question: MCQs
assessments.grading_guide: All knowledge which belong to every single block.

assessments.no_question:
1/Performance during the tour
2/Written report
assessments.grading_guide:
Practical knowledge of real situation
Research, problem-solving, planning skills, financial analysis, marketing plan, human resources management, crisis management
assessments.note:
1/ Students are required to complete a practical project that they have self-designed (based on what student got from tour project presentation 1 & 2) as part of the practical assessment, which is based on the requirements of the lecturer.

All point components of the practical project will be evaluated by lectures of the faculty as well as industry specialists. Should students choose to go the practical way, the evaluation will be based on totally the activities of students in tour, which guided in the "evaluation of Tour practical form."

2/ If students do not want to have Tour project practical, they can choose "Tour project report" instead, the written report is the detailed project version.
- The written report should be typed and double-spaced with 11-point font, and can be submitted in soft copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission
- A 0 (zero) mark will be given to any form of plagiarism detected.

assessments.no_question: Progress Presentation
assessments.grading_guide: Chapters covered in accordance to the lecture of the weeks
assessments.note:
- Students must work in groups (5-6 students/ group) to figure out basic content for a practical tour that they will submit to their instructor.
- The student's presentation content in the first session must include several key elements such as:
1/ Students need to comprehend what type of tour they wish to construct (for example: sightseeing tour, green tourism, eco-tourism, etc.), students must also examine which market will be suitable for the tour (use market analysis models such as Pestel, micro environment, macro environment, etc)
2/ Students must submit general tour information (e.g, outbound or inbound, total trip cost, packages/combos/travel products included). Furthermore, in this part, students might include a sample brochure explaining their tour to boost its vividness and appeal.
- After groups have finished presenting, the lecturer should provide relevant comments so that student groups can benefit from their experiences and be prepared to go on to the next stages.

assessments.no_question: Progress Presentation
assessments.grading_guide: Chapters covered in accordance to the lecture of the weeks
assessments.note:
- In this section, after obtaining crucial feedback from the lecturer in Part 1, student groups continue to learn and deliver the remaining content of a full tour.
- Student groups must present valuable knowledge as well as an in-depth study of a variety of essential elements in a tour program, including:
1. General information (trip name, type of tour, destination, duration, number of guests, price)
2/ Tour itinerary (detailed daily schedule, accommodation, transport, tourist attractions, experiential activities, meals, tour guide)
3/ Tour cost estimate (travel, hotel, sightseeing, food, operational, and other charges)
4) Tour marketing and communication plan (marketing channels, target customers, pricing strategy, promotion plan)
5/ Risk assessment and solutions (unnoticed risks, treatment options)

description:
Môn học Luật Hiến pháp hướng đến tìm hiểu nền tảng pháp lý cốt lõi của hệ thống pháp luật Việt Nam, tập trung vào các vấn đề trọng yếu như phương thức tổ chức và thực thi quyền lực nhà nước; mối quan hệ giữa nhà nước và công dân; và địa vị pháp lý của các cơ quan hiến định trong bộ máy nhà nước. Trong môn học này, sinh viên sẽ tìm hiểu quá trình phát triển của Hiến pháp Việt Nam, diễn giải các nguyên tắc cơ bản của chế độ chính trị, kinh tế, và làm sáng tỏ các quyền và nghĩa vụ nền tảng của công dân.

Sau khi hoàn thành môn học, về mặt kiến thức sinh viên sẽ am hiểu về cấu trúc nhà nước, các nguyên tắc hiến định, quyền con người và quyền công dân. Sinh viên cũng sẽ được học cách nhận diện và lý giải vai trò của từng cơ quan quyền lực trong các bối cảnh chính trị - xã hội cụ thể. Về mặt kỹ năng, sinh viên cũng sẽ nâng cao năng lực phân tích, so sánh các quy định pháp luật và vận dụng chúng vào những tình huống thực tiễn; được rèn luyện kỹ năng xây dựng và trình bày các lập luận pháp lý có cơ sở vững chắc; được trang bị kỹ năng vận dụng các công cụ công nghệ để phục vụ công việc một cách có trách nhiệm và đạo đức. Môn học đồng thời sẽ giúp kiến tạo thái độ làm việc chuyên nghiệp, tinh thần trách nhiệm và sự tôn trọng đối với Hiến pháp cũng như pháp luật nói chung.

Giải thích được các nội dung về chế độ chính trị - kinh tế, quyền công dân, và chức năng của các cơ quan nhà nước.
Vận dụng kiến thức hiến pháp và các công cụ công nghệ để giải quyết các tình huống pháp lý cơ bản về quyền công dân hoặc quy trình nhà nước.
Phân tích và so sánh được địa vị pháp lý và mối quan hệ giữa các cơ quan hiến định trong bộ máy nhà nước.

Phát triển năng lực tự học, làm việc độc lập, hợp tác nhóm và hình thành thái độ, đạo đức nghề nghiệp phù hợp; Vận dụng công cụ công nghệ một cách có đạo đức và trách nhiệm trong việc giải quyết các vấn đề pháp lý

Câu hỏi luận sẽ tập trung phân tích, đánh giá một vấn đề, nhận định, quan điểm về mặt lý luận của luật hiến pháp Việt Nam. Sinh viên sẽ tiến hành phân tích, đánh giá, bình luận để triển khai quan điểm của mình (phải do sinh viên tự thực hiện bằng kiến thức và khả năng của bản thân)

Phương án 2: Vấn đáp trực tiếp với giảng viên
Phần vấn đáp (theo sự chủ động đề xuất sắp xếp của giảng viên về thời gian): giảng viên tự lựa chọn phương thức triển khai phù hợp với điều kiện và thời gian phù hợp. Các câu hỏi vấn đáp bắt buộc phải nằm trong nội dung đề cương môn học. Sinh viên phải tự trả lời câu hỏi bằng kiến thức và khả năng của bản thân.

assessments.no_question:
Báo cáo, thuyết trình

'Mỗi nhóm sẽ lựa chọn một vấn đề của luật Hiến pháp để bàn luận và đưa ra giải pháp hoàn thiện quy định, chế định tương ứng trong hiến pháp.

Các lập luận phải trình bày rõ vấn đề là gì, hiện đang gặp khó khăn thách thức như thế nào, và có thể hoàn thiện thêm như thế nào. Đồng thời chỉ ra rõ việc thực hiện giải pháp như vậy sẽ hướng tới kết quả gì. Có minh chứng, so sánh dựa trên kinh nghiệm của các quốc gia và các học thuyết pháp lý tương ứng.

Sản phẩm bao gồm: một tiểu luận, một file trình chiếu, một phiên trình bày và chất vấn trên lớp với sự tham gia của tất cả các thành viên.

description:
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to corporate communications and public relations: it is for anyone with an interest in corporate communication, or anyone seeking to understand the growing importance of communication for corporations. Corporations increasingly need communication to survive, as they need to entertain relations with a variety of stakeholders to prosper. This includes not only external factors to the organization – customers, governments and civil ociety organizations, but also stakeholders within corporations themselves, such as employees, managers and investors.

The first weeks of the course focus on the basics of corporate communication: what is it, and what are its historical roots? This is important, as it demonstrates how the position of communication is increasingly considered to be managerial function – and as such should be involved in the key decision-making processes. After these introductory weeks, we turn to two core theories of corporate communication: stakeholder theory and corporate identity. These form the basis for much of the more specific and applied topics covered in the following weeks.

In addition, students will be introduced to the use of AI in corporate communications. This includes how to leverage AI tools for stakeholder analysis, media monitoring, content creation, and campaign evaluation, as well as how to address ethical and cultural considerations when adopting AI. In the last two weeks before the midterm exam, we discuss how corporations can construct communication campaigns – which will be useful as you will be tasked with creating your own communication campaign during the course. Students will also explore how AI can support the design and execution of such campaigns through audience segmentation, trend analysis, and strategic messaging assistance. After the midterm exam, we tackle specific topics of corporate communication, such as employee communications, how corporations interact with media and journalists, and how corporations should communicate in times of crisis.

learning_outcomes.details: Demonstrate a thorough understanding of corporate communication principles and related concepts, including their evolution in the digital and AI-driven era.
Comprehend the skills needed to develop impactful corporate communication strategies and/or convey them persuasively.
Develop and/or implement effective corporate communication plans.
Adopt a constructivist approach to learning that enhances creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, while leveraging AI for brainstorming and innovative solutions.

Apply learned theories and AI tools to address a real-world corporate communication challenge, demonstrating efficiency in completing projects independently or collaboratively, while maintaining ethical behavior, cultural sensitivity, and social responsibility in both human-led and AI-assisted communication practices.

assessments.grading_guide:
Case Study Analysis
Students will analyze a real-world corporate communication case (e.g., crisis response, CSR campaign, leadership communication, reputation management).
Task:
- Identify the key communication challenge(s).
- Apply corporate communication theories and frameworks to analyze the case.
- Use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Google Gemini) for supporting tasks such as sentiment analysis, social listening, reputation evalution.
- Critically evaluate the effectiveness of the adopted strategy.
- Propose alternative or improved solutions with clear justification.

Option 2 (for the constructivism approach only): Follow the lecturer's proposal.

assessments.duration:
Presentation: 20 mins per each group
Q&A: 20 mins per each group
assessments.no_question: Analyse the lastes communication challenge of a corporate and strategically develop a communication management and measurement plan to response to it.
assessments.grading_guide: Possess the ability to: (1) critically identify and analyze a communication challenge; (2) strategically apply relevant concepts and/or theories to develop a CMM plan in response to the situation; 3) Use AI tools for supporting tasks such as stakeholder mapping, competitor scanning, strategic message drafting.
assessments.note:
In class and homework. Written report (50%) & Oral presentation (50%)
CMM Plan Requirements
- Executive Summary – overview of communication challenge, objectives, and AI integration highlights.
- Situation Analysis – SWOT/PESTLE, media/stakeholder audit, AI-assisted sentiment or competitor analysis (validated by human review).
- Stakeholder Mapping & Target Audiences – AI-assisted clustering (e.g., Brandwatch, Talkwalker, ChatGPT) + team refinement.
- Communication Goal & SMART Objectives – aligned with corporate strategy.
- Key Messages – ensure message consistency, multicultural sensitivity, and ethical considerations.
- Strategies & Tactics (may covering multiple corporate communication domains):
- Integration & Channel Strategy – how AI supports consistent messaging across touchpoints.
- Budget & Resource Allocation – realistic planning, noting AI efficiency gains.
- Evaluation Plan – success indicators (trust, reputation, engagement, stakeholder sentiment), supported by AI dashboards.

Deliverables
- CMM Report (max 20 pages): Situation analysis, objectives, stakeholder mapping, strategies & tactics, integration and evaluation framework.
- Presentation Deck: 20 minutes presentation + 20 minutes Q&A.
- Reflection Section (300–500 words per group): How AI was applied, its benefits, limitations, risks, and ethical considerations.

title_vi: Các vấn đề đương đại ngành khách sạn, du lịch
title_en: Contemporary issues in hotel and tourism management
description:
This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the evolution, transformation, and future directions of the Hospitality and Tourism industries. It highlights the interconnectedness between traditional issues—such as overtourism, crisis management, destination recovery, and the sharing economy—and emerging innovations driven by Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data, and sustainable practices.

Students will explore how these forces collectively shape management, marketing, and service delivery, as well as their ethical and social implications. Key themes include environmental sustainability, digital transformation, AI in guest experience design, and data-driven decision-making.

Throughout the course, students will engage with AI-based platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Perplexity AI, Excel Copilot, and Beautiful.ai) to conduct research, analyse data, and present findings through interactive formats. The course emphasizes experiential learning, collaboration, and critical reflection, helping students bridge theory and practice to develop adaptive and future-ready competencies in the global hospitality landscape.

tools: Internet sources & AI tools ( Students are encouraged to use, Notion AI, SciSpace, and Elicit for self-study, concept explanation, and summarizing trends. For data analysis in hospitality, tools like Excel Copilot, Wolfram Alpha, and ChatGPT Code Interpreter help visualize industry statistics.)

The presentation must cover a specific aspect of the topic mentioned and demonstrate the integration of AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gemini, Copilot, etc.) to support content creation, data analysis, visualization, or idea development.

Option 2 (For Constructivism Approach only):

assessments.note:
Option 1:
For each topic, each group (4–6 students) will choose an aspect to introduce in different forms such as presentation, case study, workshop, discussion, quiz, games (crossword puzzles, Q&A..), role play... to convey knowledge to other groups in the class.
Students are encouraged to integrate AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gemini, Copilot, or other generative AI applications) to support research, idea generation, content creation, visual design, data visualization, or simulation activities during preparation and presentation.
With controversial topics, teams can conduct a 1–1 debate on an issue, optionally using AI to simulate arguments, gather contrasting perspectives, or analyze bias.

Each topic lasts 3–4 slots:

Slot 1: General understanding of topics and topic selection by groups.

Slot 2: Groups work, discuss, and use AI tools for research and content development.

Slots 3–4: Group presentations and peer learning.

Scoring recommended (see evaluation forms):

50% by lecturer (50% group, 50% individual)

50% by other groups

Follow lecturer's proposal, with an emphasis on AI-assisted exploration and reflection, where students co-construct knowledge using digital and AI-supported inquiry tools.

description:
This course focuses on the sustainability of tourism’s relationship with the natural, social, cultural and built environments. Using case studies of the environments in which tourism occurs, students explore tourism’s role in our contemporary world, both as an agent of change, and as a response to it. Creative methods are used to think differently about the future of tourism impact management.
A systematic examination of several approaches to tourism planning and policy making at both national/regional scales and from a business perspective. Develops a critical understanding of the role of decision-makers and planners on tourism development.
Approach the current status of sustainable tourism projects in the world and in Vietnam.
student_tasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final project.
- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by the instructor in class or at home and submit on time
- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose
- Promptly access to the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.details: Understand and analyse issues and challenges related to the environmental, socioeconomic impacts of tourism.
Understand and analyse issues and challenges related to the impact of tourism on local cultural heritage.
Understand and analyse the roles and interactions of stakeholders in sustainable tourism planning and development.
Analyse collaborative planning and management actions open to stakeholders for dealing with tourism-related impacts in the different environments in the future.
Apply theories, concepts and principles underpinning sustainable tourism planning and development.
Understand and apply sustainable tourism criteria for Vietnam's tourism industry and for enterprises planning in practice.
Analyse and utilise specific techniques and tools in the planning process for sustainable tourism development.
Understand and evaluate Corporate social responsibility (CSR) of enterprise for sustainable tourism
Have a sense of discipline, professional manners and a high sense of responsibility at work; Flexibility in handling situations, ability to work independently and in groups.

assessments.note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.
